audit_findings.title: Post-year-end leverage desynchronizes the earnings numerator and share denominator
audit_findings.magnitude: Debt increased $185.0 million from $34.0 million to $219.0 million; YTD interest expense increased $1.740 million; 308,985 shares were repurchased for $49.303 million YTD
audit_findings.mechanism: The equity-level OE numerator retains interest expense, but the $56.7 million anchor predates most of the additional borrowing while the denominator reflects subsequent repurchases. The issue enters through OE and shares, not a debt deduction in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: There was $34.0 million in borrowings outstanding under the revolving credit facility as of January 3, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated timing mismatch, although the exact valuation overstatement is not established. The latest filing shows substantially higher debt, higher interest expense and a lower share count. Because the additional $185.0 million of debt is more than three times anchor OE and current interest costs are already rising, aligning the numerator with the current capital structure could materially reduce value per share.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $185.0 million net borrowing to repurchases, forgivable-loan funding and other uses; calculate trailing/current normalized after-tax interest expense; then rerun all scenarios with an OE numerator and fully diluted share count measured on the same date.

audit_findings.title: Forgivable-loan advances may be recurring talent investment not captured by current compensation expense
audit_findings.magnitude: Fiscal-2025 forgivable-loan cash use was $53.411 million, equal to 94.2% of the $56.7 million anchor; 2026 YTD cash use was $58.263 million, equal to 102.8% of the anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Any normalized cash advances required to maintain the consultant base or support forecast growth enter as an OE reinvestment requirement to the extent they exceed the amortization already included in compensation expense.
audit_findings.evidence: Offsetting these sources of cash for operating activities included, a $25.7 million increase in accounts receivable and unbilled receivables, a $20.5 million decrease in lease liabilities, a $53.4 million increase in forgivable loans, (comprised of $86.0 million of forgivable loan issuances, net of repayments, offset by $32.6 million of forgivable loan amortization), and a $4.4 million decrease in prepaid expenses and other current assets.
audit_findings.explanation: The recurrence and scale are demonstrated: advances were $87.909 million in fiscal 2025 and $81.974 million in the following half-year, while the loan balance rose from $55.492 million to $141.595 million over eighteen months. What remains unresolved is how much represents temporary timing or growth investment versus maintenance spending. Even a fraction of the observed net cash use could materially reduce the $56.7 million distributable-OE anchor, so the issue is open and material rather than merely speculative.
audit_findings.action: Obtain cohort-level advances, repayments, reclassifications, forgiveness and amortization schedules; separate maintenance hiring and retention from growth investment; estimate a normalized cash requirement; and rerun without double-counting amounts already recognized through amortization.

audit_findings.title: The latest-actual anchor contains an extra operating week
audit_findings.magnitude: Mechanical 52/53 normalization reduces anchor OE by $1.07 million, or 1.89%; indicated value reductions are approximately $1.96, $2.76 and $3.05 per share for bear, base and bull, respectively
audit_findings.mechanism: The extra week inflates the OE anchor and therefore every forecast operating cash flow and terminal value; it does not affect shares or the cash bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Fiscal 2025 was a 53-week year, and fiscal 2024 was a 52-week year.
audit_findings.explanation: The 53-week year is demonstrated, but its mechanical scale is small relative to the valuation spreads. A proportional normalization would reduce base value from $149.86 to about $147.10 per share and the 30% buy-below level from $104.90 to about $102.97. Bull value would fall from $166.83 to about $163.78, leaving it further below the $170.91 market price. This does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether the extra week had approximately normal revenue and margins, then apply a 52-week normalization to fiscal-2025 OE for presentation accuracy; no conclusion-level rerun is required unless the week was unusually profitable.

audit_findings.title: Part of the anchor depends on subjective fixed-price cost-to-complete estimates
audit_findings.mechanism: Cost-to-complete estimate errors can shift fixed-price revenue and profit between periods, altering anchor OE and potentially the sustainable margin or growth assumptions.
audit_findings.evidence: We identified the Company’s estimates of total costs to complete a performance obligation for performance obligations in a fixed-price arrangement that are partially satisfied at the balance sheet date as a critical audit matter.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved estimation possibility, not a demonstrated accounting error. Fixed-price work represented 17% of fiscal-2025 revenue, but the filing does not quantify the profit recognized on incomplete engagements, estimate revisions or any bias in management's estimates. The auditor tested relevant controls, historical estimation ability and subsequent costs and still issued an unqualified opinion. Nevertheless, because the affected profit pool is unknown and fixed-price revenue subsequently increased to 20% YTD and 23% in the latest quarter, the record cannot establish that the exposure is immaterial.
audit_findings.action: Obtain fixed-price engagement gross profit, remaining-cost estimates, subsequent actual costs, estimate revisions, prior-period true-ups and loss-contract charges; quantify their effect on fiscal-2025 OE and rerun only if normalized OE or sustainable margins change materially.
